record.title: ReAgent reports improved paper–repository consistency audits on one research-agent benchmark
record.summary: ReAgent combines static inspection of paper claims against repository implementations with dynamic execution evidence. On 96 auditable repositories from a screened set of 188 AutoSOTA agent-generated paper–repository pairs, the authors report 70.83% overall audit accuracy versus 35.42% for Codex using GPT-5.4 and manually established ground truth. Ninety-two repositories were excluded, mostly because datasets or checkpoints were unavailable. The result is author-reported and limited to one platform.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ReAgent combines static claim-to-code review with dynamic experiment execution and evidence collection to assess consistency between research documents and repositories.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 96 auditable AutoSOTA repositories, the paper reports 70.83% overall audit accuracy for ReAgent versus 35.42% for Codex against manually established ground truth.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Repository consistency does not establish scientific validity or novelty, and the benchmark does not establish generalization beyond AutoSOTA.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported benchmark comparison has not been independently reproduced.
Generalization beyond the AutoSOTA repository collection is unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If automated checks can detect when research claims diverge from their code and execution artifacts, they could improve auditability as agents produce more research outputs. The evidence is one author-evaluated benchmark on an auditable subset and does not establish scientific validity or broad generalization.
limitations: All results are reported by the authors; the research desk did not independently reproduce the benchmark.
The 96 audited repositories come from one platform; 92 of 188 screened pairs were excluded, mostly because assets were unavailable.
The audit evaluates paper–repository consistency, not the scientific validity or novelty of methods or conclusions.
Generalization to other agent platforms and human-authored research artifacts is unknown.
brief.summary: ReAgent combines static inspection of paper claims against repository implementations with dynamic execution evidence. On 96 auditable repositories from a screened set of 188 AutoSOTA agent-generated paper–repository pairs, the authors report 70.83% overall audit accuracy versus 35.42% for Codex using GPT-5.4 and manually established ground truth. Ninety-two repositories were excluded, mostly because datasets or checkpoints were unavailable. The result is author-reported and limited to one platform.

technical.claimed_result: Among 96 auditable AutoSOTA repositories, the authors report 70.83% overall audit accuracy versus 35.42% for Codex. Dynamic verification accuracy is reported as 90.63%; 33 repositories reproduced their reported metrics, but only 25 passed both static consistency and reproduction.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1 paper reports the benchmark, manually established labels and comparison results. the research desk did not run the system or independently validate the benchmark.
technical.mechanism: Static verification extracts claim contracts and aligns them with implementation evidence; dynamic verification plans and runs experiments, records execution traces, and distinguishes matched, mismatched, blocked and not-reproduced outcomes.
technical.regime: A manually audited, auditable subset of AutoSOTA: 96 of 188 agent-generated paper–repository pairs. Ninety-two were excluded, mostly for unavailable datasets or checkpoints. Evaluation used manually established ground truth and GPT-5.4 across compared methods.
technical.strongest_baseline: Codex using the same GPT-5.4 model and task inputs; the paper reports 35.42% overall audit accuracy versus ReAgent’s 70.83%.

brief.title: ReAgent reports improved paper–repository consistency audits on one research-agent benchmark
brief.why_it_matters: As research agents generate papers, code and experiments together, an audit that checks both implementation fidelity and execution evidence could catch unsupported claims that either static review or successful reproduction alone misses. This benchmark concerns artifact consistency; it does not certify whether a method or conclusion is scientifically valid.
